root_idea.summary: The root centers on twisting or turning something away from its straight direction.
root_idea.development: From physical twisting and turning, the root develops usages for diverting someone from a matter, turning the face or regard aside, removing a covering, and related derived descriptions.

senses.definition: To turn or divert someone from a direction, matter, or course; to turn someone away from something.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction with عَنْ, the object is caused to turn away from a matter or course.

senses.definition: To turn one's face or regard aside; to look back or turn to another direction.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quranic occurrences, the form appears in a prohibitive construction meaning not to look back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To twist, wring, or turn a person or thing away from its proper direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes twisting or wringing the neck and turning something about, such as a cow turning fresh herb with its tongue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take someone away suddenly, especially by death.
To turn someone from his opinion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended usage concerning a person's view or judgment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To beat camels, sheep, or goats indiscriminately, without caring which animal is struck.
To utter or send forth words without caring what they mean.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage concerning careless or unintelligible speech.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stir a thing about and over, as flour is stirred with clarified butter.
To remove or pull off the peel or rind from a tree, twig, or branch.
To put feathers on an arrow in an uneven or mismatched arrangement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feathers are attached without making them equal, uniform, or well-composed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pay no regard or attention to someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Expressed in the conventional negative construction ما التفت إليه.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Half of a thing; its side or flank.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense is also reflected in a phrase meaning not to look toward someone's side.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cow or bull.
A woman who is stupid, foolish, or of little sense.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine referent is part of the lexical definition in this entry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The vulva of a lioness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In Egyptian usage, the rape plant, Brassica napus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry reports uncertainty about whether this word is Arabic and records an assertion that it is Nabataean.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A condition in which one horn of a he-goat is twisted over the other.
A man who repeatedly beats his camels, sheep, or goats without caring which animal he strikes.
A woman who looks aside frequently or whose regard is readily diverted.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions include looking toward a speaking man, not keeping the eyes fixed on one place, and using glances or signs. The term is also applied to a woman distracted by a child from a previous husband while married to another man.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that is restless during milking, looks aside at the milker, and bites him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description includes her yielding milk after being struck; the epithet is proverbially extended to a disobedient person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Difficult or stubborn in disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This meaning is reported alongside contrary lexical testimony in the same discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman marked by crookedness and constriction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation explains the description as involving التواء وانقباض.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who goes to calumniate or slander.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare and obscure transmitted gloss.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thick gruel or stew made by cooking and thickening a prepared liquid with flour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is connected with stirring or turning the mixture; the preparation is also described as a thick عصيدة or a broth resembling حَيْس.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong-handed, able to hoist or wring someone who grapples with him.
A he-goat having crooked or twisted horns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The corresponding feminine form لَفْتَاءُ is used for a she-goat with crooked horns.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having distorted or cross-directed eyes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine form لَفْتَاءُ is used for a woman with this feature.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stupid, foolish, or of little sense; in some reports, also difficult or stubborn in disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry records variation in the transmitted wording and related interpretation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Left-handed; working with the left hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a dialectal usage of Temeem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The highest bone at the place where the head joins the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical noun.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Illustrative phrase only; it adds no independent lexical branch.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form VIII discussion.

cautions: The Mufradat entry reports the expression لِتَلْفِتَنا with the citation Yūnus 87, while the supplied QAC occurrence is securely located at 10:78:3; the artifact uses the QAC location and does not normalize the conflicting citation.
The plant sense under لِفْتٌ is reported with uncertainty about its Arabic status and with a claim of Nabataean origin.
The meanings of لَفُوتٌ and أَلْفَتُ include transmitted lexical disagreement or obscure reports, which are retained as such.
